should_fire.text: I have a bunch of Jira tickets and commit messages for this sprint, can you turn them into something I can send to customers describing what's new and what got fixed?
should_fire.notes: Directly matches the target's core purpose of converting raw changes into client-facing release notes, distinct from rival 6's general external-writing rules.

should_fire.text: I have a list of internal ticket fixes for this sprint — can you turn it into short release notes our customers will actually see in the changelog?
should_fire.notes: This targets the core purpose of the skill (client-facing release notes from a raw change list) rather than rival 6's general external-writing rules, since it needs the specific structure (headings, word limit, ticket redaction).

should_fire.text: Draft the changelog entry for this release — group the bug fixes and new features under headings, keep it super short, and don't leak any of our internal branch or module names.
should_fire.notes: This asks for the precise Added/Fixed structure and word-limit/internal-name redaction that only the target documentation specifies, distinguishing it from rival 6's generic 'writing for outsiders' rules which lack headings, word counts, or bullet format.

should_not_fire.text: We're emailing the top 3 clients tonight about the outage postmortem — can you write it up: what happened, then what it means for them, with the latency numbers and baseline included?
should_not_fire.notes: The request mentions client-facing writing about changes/incidents, which superficially overlaps with the TARGET's 'release notes a client can read' framing, but it's actually an external incident postmortem needing claim-per-sentence rigor and sourced numbers — a job for the general external-communication rival, not the strict Added/Fixed release-notes template.

should_not_fire.text: Can you pull the list of every bug fixed this sprint from the tickets table so I can turn it into notes for the client?
should_not_fire.notes: It name-drops 'fixed' and 'client notes,' echoing the TARGET's Added/Fixed release-notes format, but the actual ask is to query a database table for ticket data — that's the database-access rival's job, and only after that would formatting even become relevant.
